meta.version_detail: 26.3 released September 15, 2026 (first snapshot June 23, 2026). Next version 26.4 is in snapshots (26.4 Snapshot 10 as of the wiki on 2026-11-24).
sources: https://minecraft.wiki/w/Trading (rendered via api.php?action=parse; trade tables come from the wiki trade database)
meta.rebalance: Default in 26.3 (since Java 1.21.5): rebalanced cartographer (biome-specific village maps, jungle/swamp explorer maps, paper/glass pane 12 uses) and rebalanced wandering trader (buy trades, 2+2+5 offers, cheaper prices). Still experimental (Villager Trade Rebalance data pack): biome-specific librarian enchanted books and biome-specific armorers. Butcher, cleric, farmer, fisherman, fletcher, leatherworker, mason, shepherd, toolsmith and weaponsmith are unchanged by the rebalance.
meta.format_notes: Counts: "count" is a fixed amount, or the minimum when "count_max" is present (a random price picked when the trade unlocks). "chance_java" is the wiki's Java chance that a given trade is one of the level's picks (values over 100% are the expected number of offers from a multi-trade group). Item "<color>_x" means one separate trade per dye color. Prices shown are base prices before demand/reputation/Hero of the Village. Java Edition only. Nitwits and unemployed villagers (and babies) have no trades.
unsure: Wandering trader price multipliers and whether each wandering trade is exactly equally likely (wiki marks it "verify").
Item ids sulfur_spike, shelf_mushroom, poplar_log, poplar_sapling are inferred from wiki names (items added in 26.2/26.3).
The wiki rebalance page still lists cartographer glass pane max uses 16 in its old table; the Trading page and history say 12 since 1.21.5 (12 used).

mechanics.name: Levels and villager XP
mechanics.text: Novice 0, apprentice 10, journeyman 70, expert 150, master 250 total villager XP. Each trade adds its "xp" value. Java: each level unlocks up to 2 new trades picked at random from that level's pool (all if the pool has 2 or fewer); max 10 trades. Exception: master librarians pick 3 (since 26.1). Leveling up gives the villager 10 s of Regeneration I. Master trades still add XP but do nothing.

mechanics.name: Player XP from trading
mechanics.text: Every villager trade gives the player 3-6 XP, plus 5 XP if the trade levels the villager up (8-11 instead of 3-6 while the villager is willing to breed, per the Villager page). Wandering trader trades also give player XP.

mechanics.name: Locking trades
mechanics.text: An unemployed villager takes a profession by claiming a job site block. A novice that has never been traded with loses the job if its job site is removed, and re-rolls its trades when it reclaims one (and periodically while it has no XP). One trade locks the profession and offers forever.

mechanics.name: Restocking
mechanics.text: Each trade has max uses. Villagers restock all trades when they work at their job site, up to twice per Minecraft day; after 2 restocks within 10 minutes a villager waits at least 10 minutes. (Bedrock also needs a bed; not Java.)

mechanics.name: Price formula (Java)
mechanics.text: Final price = clamp( floor(p*(m*max(0,d)+1)) - floor(m*r) - [Hero] max(1, floor(p*(0.3+0.0625*(h-1)))), 1, stack size ), where p = base price, m = price multiplier, d = demand, r = reputation, h = Hero of the Village level. Only the first wanted item changes price; the second item and the output never change.

mechanics.name: Demand
mechanics.text: Tracked per trade. Starts at minus 2x the trade's max uses. At each restock: demand = demand - max uses + 2x uses actually made. When demand is positive the price rises by floor(base price * multiplier * demand). Not trading lets it fall back.

mechanics.name: Reputation / gossip
mechanics.text: Reputation = sum of gossip value x weight, per player per villager. trading: +4 per trade, max 25, weight 1, decays 2 per 20 min. Curing: major_positive +20 (max 20, weight 5, never decays, never shared) and minor_positive +25 (max 25, weight 1, decays 1 per 20 min). Attacking: minor_negative +25 (max 200, weight -1). Killing a nearby villager: major_negative +25 (max 100, weight -5, spreads to villagers that see it within 16 blocks). Price drops by floor(multiplier x reputation); in Java negative reputation can raise prices. Gossip spreads between villagers minus a sharing cost; decay is every 20 real minutes regardless of sleep.

mechanics.name: Zombie cure discount
mechanics.text: Curing a zombie villager gives you major_positive 20 + minor_positive 25 = reputation 125 at first (20x5 + 25), so price drops by floor(125 x multiplier): about 6 emeralds off a 0.05 trade and 25 off a 0.2 trade (always at least 1 left). The 100-point major part is permanent; the 25 minor part decays. Since Java 1.20.2 the discount is given only the first time a villager is cured: re-zombifying and curing again no longer stacks (bug MC-181190 fixed). Villagers that already had stacked discounts kept them. Reasoned arithmetic from the wiki gossip table.

mechanics.name: Hero of the Village
mechanics.text: From winning a raid. Cuts every villager price by 30% at level I plus 6.25% per extra level (up to 55% at V) of the base price, rounded down but at least 1 item. Not scaled by the price multiplier. Stacks with reputation discounts.

mechanics.name: Buying items from players
mechanics.text: Villagers ignore extra item data when buying: renamed or enchanted items, and lodestone compasses for compass trades, are accepted.

mechanics.name: Data-driven trades
mechanics.text: Since Java 26.1 villager trades are defined by data packs (villager trade definitions), so servers or data packs can change these tables.

mechanics.name: Non-trading villagers
mechanics.text: Nitwits (green coat) never get a profession; unemployed villagers and babies cannot trade. In Java they grunt and shake their head when clicked.

wandering_trader.notes: Always 9 offers in this order: 2 buy trades, 2 special sell trades, 5 ordinary sell trades, each picked with equal chance within its table (wiki flags "each trade is equally likely" as needing verification). This is the rebalanced trader, default since Java 1.21.5. It has no levels and no villager XP; the wiki hides price multipliers for it (null here). Trades give the player XP. Since 26.1 it also sells name tags (1 emerald). Its stock does not restock (inferred: it has no job site).

experimental.notes: Villager Trade Rebalance experiment (still experimental in Java 26.3; enable the experiment data pack at world creation). Books depend on the villager biome type. Common books (novice-expert, random level): desert Fire Protection, Thorns, Infinity; plains Punch, Smite, Bane of Arthropods; savanna Knockback, Curse of Binding, Sweeping Edge; snowy Aqua Affinity, Looting, Frost Walker; taiga Blast Protection, Fire Aspect, Flame; jungle Feather Falling, Projectile Protection, Power; swamp Depth Strider, Respiration, Curse of Vanishing. Special book (master only, fixed level): desert Efficiency III, plains Protection III, savanna Sharpness III, snowy Silk Touch, taiga Fortune II, jungle Unbreaking II, swamp Mending. Crossbow, fishing rod, trident, mace and spear enchantments cannot be traded. Jungle and swamp villages do not generate naturally: breed or cure villagers in those biomes. The experiment also raises Mending/Unbreaking/Efficiency/Quick Charge book odds in some structure loot.

trades.notes: The enchantment is chosen randomly from the "Common" enchantments listed on the table below according to the biome of the villagers. Every level of these enchantments has an equal chance to be chosen, meaning high-level enchantments are as likely as low-level enchantments. It is possible for a librarian to sell the same book more than once. Price 2+3*level to 6+13*level emeralds, doubled for treasure, capped at 64.
